3.	Legend has it that a wandering people had been told by their patron god to settle wherever they finally saw an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus, devouring a serpent. In 1325 CE they saw the sign on a small island in the middle of a shallow lake, and they founded their city there. By the time Hernán Cortés arrived in 1519, the city of X had become one of the largest cities on earth, with elaborate causeways, aqueducts, and floating chinampa gardens. Cortés besieged and demolished it in 1521, then built his Spanish colonial capital Y on top of the ruins; the lake was drained over the following centuries. As a result, Y is sinking by several centimeters every year as the old lakebed continues to compact under the weight of the city. ID X (10 points) and Y (10 points). ‎<attached: 00137050-PHOTO-2026-04-30-09-12-11.jpg>
Answers: X= Tenochtitlán, Y=Mexico City (Ciudad de México), Mexico

4.	According to local legend, this city was founded by Shem, the son of Noah, who walked south after the Great Flood and laid out its first walls. This is one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited human settlements. Its Old City — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — is famous for its remarkable multi-story tower houses, built of rammed earth and dark basalt and decorated with delicate white gypsum tracings around every window. Since 2014, the city has been a battle zone in a civil war. Name this capital city in the southwestern corner of the Arabian Peninsula (10 points). ‎<attached: 00137062-PHOTO-2026-04-30-09-13-56.jpg>
